messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about one‑tenth of atmospheric pressure), pure water freezes at roughly **–2 °C**.  
This comes from the fact that the solid–liquid coexistence curve has a negative slope: as pressure drops below 1 atm, the equilibrium temperature between ice and liquid water shifts downward by about 0.5 °C per 50 kPa drop. So at 10 kPa you get a freezing point near –2 °C.
